meals: Beef and corn burritos with cheese and salsa verde
green curry with spinach and basa fillets
weeks.notes: Went with burritos because pantry only had a few ingredients at the time, and they only needed to be seasoned with taco seasoning. Went with eggs with oatmeal and quesadillas because these are both very quick to prepare.
weeks.feedback: Spinach came out with a poor texture in the curry, burritos were fine, I enjoyed the simplicity of the quesadillas and eggs with oatmeal -- this is a good benchmark for the level of difficulty I want for the quick meals each week. Note that I can handle more complexity on the meal prep meals.

meals: Sheet Pan Salmon with Potatoes and Broccoli
weeks.notes: The two meal-prep meals this week are Beef Chili with Rice and Sheet Pan Salmon with Potatoes and Broccoli. The chili leans into the pantry's strong spice lineup (cumin, cayenne, sweet paprika, garlic) and is a proven crowd-pleaser from the example recipes — but it has not appeared in the recent backlog, so it's a clean rotation entry. It hits roughly 1,050 calories per serving with a solid protein contribution from beef and beans, and covers the iron and legume bases well. The sheet pan salmon is the second new meal, bringing a completely different protein, cooking method, and flavour profile. The only new staple it calls for is Dijon mustard, keeping new purchases to a minimum. Salmon with potatoes and broccoli lands around 1,100 calories per serving and is rich in omega-3s, iron, and vegetables. Together, the two meal-preps generate 8 servings and account for roughly 8,600–8,800 calories of the weekly 17,000–17,500 target, with snacks, eating out, and the quick meals filling the remainder. For the two quick meals, frozen dumplings with broccoli and cheese quesadillas with salsa were chosen — both are under 15 minutes, few dishes, and match exactly the simplicity praised in last week's feedback ("this is a good benchmark for the level of difficulty I want for the quick meals"). Last week's curry used spinach and the texture was called out as poor, so spinach-in-broth combinations have been avoided this week. The green curry with basa from last week is excluded per the two-week recency rule. Dijon mustard is the one new pantry addition introduced this week; soy sauce for the dumplings is included as a fresh purchase since it doesn't appear in the snapshot. Snacks follow the usual rotation with a few variety additions (trail mix, sourdough with hummus, cucumbers) alongside the regulars.
weeks.feedback: Everything was good, chili is always one of my mainstays and I usually make it every 3 weeks or so. I would like to branch out a little more with the snacks

meals: Slow-Cooked Soy Pork with Mushrooms and Rice
Chicken and Sweet Potato Coconut Curry
weeks.notes: This week's two meal-prep meals are Slow-Cooked Soy Pork with Mushrooms and Rice, and Chicken and Sweet Potato Coconut Curry. The soy pork is drawn directly from the user's example recipes and hasn't appeared in the recent backlog, making it a clean rotation entry — it's a low-effort slow cooker dish (no chopping needed beyond optional mushroom prep), hits around 1,100 cal/serving with good protein, and uses pantry staples (garlic, pepper, salsa) alongside just two new sauces: soy sauce and Worcestershire. Soy sauce was needed last week for dumplings and isn't in the snapshot yet, so it's a natural addition. The chicken coconut curry is the week's genuinely new rotation entry — it avoids the green curry + spinach combination that drew criticism for texture last week, and instead uses sweet potato and broccoli florets as the vegetable base (both hold their texture well in a braise). The spice profile leans on the pantry's strong Indian spice lineup (garam masala, cumin, sweet paprika, cayenne) with coconut milk for richness, landing around 1,150 cal/serving and offering good iron and vegetable variety. No new staples are introduced for this meal — everything except the fresh ingredients is already on hand. Together the two meal-preps produce 8 servings covering roughly 8,900–9,000 calories. For the quick meals, frozen dumplings with broccoli and cheese quesadillas with salsa are retained — both were explicitly praised as the right complexity benchmark last week, and the feedback didn't suggest replacing them. They remain the simplest, fastest options that match the user's stated quick-meal standard. The snack selection has been broadened this week in response to last week's feedback requesting more snack variety: alongside the usuals (cashews, rice crackers, sourdough + hummus, yoghurt, frozen mango, bananas, peanut butter), new additions include dark chocolate, dried apricots, sunflower seeds, corn thins, rice cakes, and crunchy pickles — all distinct in texture and flavour profile. Trail mix and frozen blueberries have been rotated out this week to make room. Beef chili is excluded per the three-week cadence the user mentioned (made last week); sheet pan salmon is excluded under the two-week recency rule. The green curry with basa is also still excluded per recency.
weeks.feedback: good. add slightly more variety with the quick meals.
